difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-dualizing, for X of finite type over S and two finite open coverings U and V of X by schemes separated over S, the lemma asserts that if a dualizing complex normalised relative to omega_S^bullet and U exists then one normalised relative to omega_S^bullet and V exists, and that the two are canonically isomorphic (statement lines 5347-5357). The proof reduces to the case where U is given by U_1, ..., U_n and V by U_1, ..., U_{n+m}, and then to m = 1: passing from V to U is achieved by forgetting the extra local isomorphism, while the converse requires constructing a map alpha_{n+1} : K|_{U_{n+1}} -> omega_{n+1}^bullet for a complex (K, alpha_i) normalised for U (proof lines 5359-5374). For this the proof observes that U_{n+1} = union of U_i cap U_{n+1} is an open covering and that both (K|_{U_{n+1}}, alpha_i|_{U_i cap U_{n+1}}) and, by the cocycle gluing condition equation labelled item-cocycle-glueing, the pair (omega_{n+1}^bullet|_{U_{n+1}}, phi_{n+1 i}) are dualizing complexes normalised relative to omega_S^bullet and that covering; Lemma labelled lemma-good-dualizing-unique then gives a unique compatible isomorphism alpha_{n+1}, and the author closes by calling it a pleasant exercise that it satisfies the required property (proof lines 5376-5389). Reducing the two coverings to a one element extension and manufacturing the missing local isomorphism by uniqueness on the overlap is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
